instructions: About 8 1/2 hours before dinner, stir together the rub in a small bowl: 1 tbsp brown sugar, the 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp of the onion powder, the 1/2 tsp garlic powder, the 1/4 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp of the mustard powder, 1/2 tsp of the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper.
Pat the 2 lb pork dry with paper towels. If it's one thick piece, cut it in half. Rub the spice mix all over every side.
Put the pork in the slow cooker and pour the 1/2 cup apple juice around it. Cover and cook on low for 8 hours. No peeking. It's ready when it falls apart as you press it with a fork.
About 40 minutes before dinner, heat the oven to 350°F. Ladle 1/2 cup of the juices from the slow cooker into a medium saucepan.

Add the 1 cup ketchup, 3 tbsp of the vinegar, 1/4 cup brown sugar, the 1 tsp Worcestershire, the remaining 1/2 tsp onion powder, the remaining 1/2 tsp mustard powder and the remaining 1/2 tsp pepper. Whisk it smooth and bring it to a simmer over medium.
Turn the heat down to low, partly cover the pan and simmer the sauce gently for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's thick enough to coat a spoon. Keep the lid partly on. It spatters.
Meanwhile, lift the pork out of the slow cooker onto a rimmed baking sheet. Roast it for 20 minutes, until the outside is browned and the edges are a little crisp.
While the pork roasts, make the slaw. In a large bowl, stir together the 1/3 cup mayonnaise, the last 1 tbsp vinegar and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt. Add the coleslaw mix and toss until it's coated.
Shred the pork on the baking sheet with two forks, pulling out and throwing away any soft pieces of fat.
Pour about two thirds of the sauce over the pork and toss until it's coated. Pour the rest of the sauce into a small bowl.
Split the 4 buns and toast them cut side down in a dry skillet over medium for about 1 minute, until golden.
Taste the pork. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the pork piled on the toasted buns with the coleslaw on top and the extra sauce on the side.
advance_prep_notes: start the slow cooker about 8 1/2 hours before dinner
method_notes: Both cook a pork shoulder low and slow until it shreds, then coat it in a ketchup, cider vinegar and brown sugar barbecue sauce and serve it on rolls with coleslaw. RecipeTin Eats (the lead) rubs the pork with a sweet paprika spice mix, slow cooks it in apple cider or apple juice for 8 hours on low, browns it in the oven before shredding and simmers a separate sauce made with some of the cooking juices. Simply Scratch sears the pork in a skillet first and cooks it right in the sauce with onion and chipotle powder. This one follows the lead for a 2 lb shoulder, leaves out the lead's splash of lemon juice in the sauce and dresses bagged coleslaw mix with mayonnaise and vinegar.
